requirement_text: International applicants to UCM must request 'Verificación' and 'Calificación de Admisión' of their secondary/baccalaureate studies through UNED's UNEDasiss service before applying for admission.
source_authority_note: venalacomplu.ucm.es is UCM's own official international-admissions subdomain; .es domain, not .edu/.ac/.gov, so fails the literal gate despite being UCM's direct official page.

requirement_text: UCM applicants using foreign qualifications may pursue one or more compatible options to raise their admission score: (1) PCE (Pruebas de Competencias Específicas) exams administered by UNED; (2) subject recognition — UNED validation of previously-completed subjects that weight toward the chosen degree, limited to courses 'cursadas o superadas en los tres años anteriores', and explicitly NOT available for students coming from Colombian or UK education systems; (3) the optional/specific phase of the PAU at any Spanish public university. The system then applies 'las dos mejores calificaciones' (the two best grades) among the relevant weighted subjects.
source_authority_note: UCM's own official international-admissions subdomain; .es domain, not .edu/.ac/.gov.
researcher_notes: The Colombia/UK subject-recognition exclusion is a specific, actionable carve-out ORYN should surface for students from those two systems specifically.

requirement_text: Non-Spanish-speaking students from non-Spanish-speaking education systems must demonstrate Spanish proficiency at B2 level ('un nivel B2 de español') to access UCM.
source_authority_note: UCM's own official admissions page; .es domain, not .edu/.ac/.gov.
limitations: Exact stage this is checked at (pre-registration vs. enrollment/matriculation) is not fully specified on this page.

requirement_text: The UNED accreditation document (Acreditación) used for admission to UCM remains valid for two years from its date of issuance.
source_authority_note: UCM's own official admissions page; .es domain, not .edu/.ac/.gov.
researcher_notes: Matches the identical figure independently confirmed on the general Spain-system UNEDasiss fact (REQ-2026-08-21-0007).

requirement_text: UCM publishes cut-off marks across six access groups, defined verbatim as: 'Grupo 1: Pruebas de acceso a la Universidad y equivalentes // Formación Profesional y equivalentes'; 'Grupo 2: Titulados o equivalentes'; 'Grupo 3: Mayores de 25 años'; 'Grupo 4: Mayores de 45'; 'Grupo 5: Mayores de 40 con experiencia profesional'; 'Grupo 6: Bachillerato homologado sin prueba de acceso'.
source_authority_note: UCM's own official notas de corte page; .es domain, not .edu/.ac/.gov.
limitations: UCM's Grupo 1 label ('Pruebas de acceso a la Universidad y equivalentes // FP y equivalentes') does NOT explicitly name UNED/UNEDasiss accreditation the way UC3M's equivalent group definition does ('Acceso con Bachillerato, Formación Profesional y Acreditación UNED Assis' — see UC3M file). Grupo 6 ('Bachillerato homologado sin prueba de acceso') is a plausible alternative home for some UNEDasiss-accredited students but this was not confirmed either. Multiple targeted searches and direct page fetches could not locate an explicit UCM statement of which numbered group UNEDasiss/international students compete within.
researcher_notes: FLAGGING FOR REVIEW: this materially affects how to interpret the notas de corte recorded below (REQ-2026-08-21-2006 through 2010) for ORYN's international users specifically. It is NOT certain that 'Grupo 1' cut-offs are the right competitive benchmark for a UNEDasiss-accredited applicant at UCM, unlike at UC3M where Group 1 explicitly includes UNED-accredited students. The Grupo 1 figures are recorded anyway since they are the most likely candidate (structurally parallels UC3M's Group 1 and covers the largest applicant pool, and is explicitly the group labeled 'Grupo 1' consistent with how UC3M names its equivalent group) but this should be verified directly with UCM admissions before ORYN presents it to students as a precise benchmark.

requirement_text: 2026-2027 admission cycle nota de corte (Grupo 1, ordinary admission) for Medicina at UCM: 13,053 (out of 14). This is the score achieved by the LAST student admitted into this programme's Group 1 pool that cycle — a retrospective competitive outcome, NOT a published minimum threshold a student must clear in advance.
source_authority_note: UCM's own official notas de corte page; .es domain, not .edu/.ac/.gov.
limitations: Specific to the 2026-2027 cycle; cut-offs move annually based on demand and available seats. UCM's own page states: 'Las notas de corte de años anteriores son una orientación sobre la nota que el estudiante debe alcanzar para acceder a un grado determinado' — i.e. even UCM frames prior-year figures as indicative only, not a guarantee. ALSO SEE REQ-2026-08-21-2005: whether 'Grupo 1' is the correct benchmark group for a UNEDasiss-accredited international applicant at UCM specifically (as opposed to a domestic Bachillerato/EvAU applicant) could not be confirmed.
researcher_notes: OUTCOME DATA, NOT A REQUIREMENT: this number reflects competitive demand for the 2026-2027 cycle specifically. Whoever maps this into ORYN's database should keep it in a clearly distinct field/fact-type from actual stated requirement thresholds (e.g. a 'historical_cutoff' type), not conflated with 'minimum_grade'.

requirement_text: UCM applicants (via Madrid's Distrito Único system) may list up to 12 degree programmes by preference order in a single online application covering all six Madrid public universities; only one submission per applicant is allowed district-wide, and the preference order cannot be modified once the application window closes ('No será posible modificar dicho orden una vez cerrado el plazo').
source_authority_note: UCM's own official international-admissions subdomain; .es domain, not .edu/.ac/.gov.
researcher_notes: Applies district-wide (all six Madrid public universities including UC3M), not solely to UCM, but sourced here from UCM's own page.

requirement_text: UCM's 'Early Admission 2026-27' pathway targets applicants from foreign education systems whose entire family resides outside Spain. Three eligible categories: (1) students with non-EU-country qualifications equivalent to advanced Spanish secondary education; (2) students with equivalent credentials from EU member states or reciprocity-agreement countries; (3) International Baccalaureate (IB) or European Baccalaureate (EB) holders from EU or reciprocity-agreement countries (named: Andorra, China, Colombia, Liechtenstein, Norway, Switzerland, UK). Admission additionally requires completion of UCM's 'university skills course / International Foundation Program' or an equivalent Foundation Program at an institution holding a collaboration agreement with UCM.
source_authority_note: UCM's own official Early Admission program page; .es domain, not .edu/.ac/.gov.
limitations: Page does not specify a minimum admission score/threshold for this pathway. Consult Annex I of the official call (not independently fetched in this research pass) for seat availability by programme. Contact given: earlyadmissiongrado@ucm.es.
researcher_notes: This pathway appears specific to UCM (not confirmed as offered by UC3M) — a genuine point of differentiation between the two universities worth flagging to ORYN's international applicants who live entirely outside Spain.

limitations: Distinct pathway/calendar from UCM's general Distrito Único preinscripción window (see DL-2026-08-21-2014) — do not conflate the two.

limitations: UNEDasiss's own 'fechas_clave' page (https://unedasiss.uned.es/fechas_clave) independently states '7 de julio de 2026' as the general deadline to apply for admission to Spanish public universities for the 2026/2027 cycle — one day LATER than UCM's own stated 6 July/14:00 cutoff.
